subject: Acme pricing / token-volume follow-up and invoice estimate
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmecorp.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme pricing / token-volume follow-up and invoice estimate

Hi Alice / Bob — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- High-level: Acme is planning to ship two LLM-powered features in H2: (1) an in-product assistant (avg. response ~300 tokens) and (2) a nightly batch reranker for search (shorter outputs, avg ~40 tokens).
- Expected traffic: you mentioned a starting range of ~200M–400M tokens/month, with potential to scale to ~800M+ over 12 months depending on adoption.
- Key constraints: procurement prefers a predictable unit price and committed volume discounts; security/compliance checklist in progress (we can provide SOC2 docs).

Can you confirm the monthly token range you want us to use for an initial invoice estimate (best / expected / upside)? Also, what target $/1M tokens are you budgeting for (or a budget range)? That will help me align the proposal and discount tiers.

I'll put together a short invoice estimate and a simple cost model (spreadsheet) showing unit economics (compute, caching, support) and send it over — aim to have that to you by Friday.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the monthly token bands and target $/1M tokens
- I send estimate + cost model
- If numbers look good, schedule a technical walkthrough w/ Marissa (SE) and David (SRE) next week

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Sean
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

---
Attachment: (none)
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmecorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Acme pricing / token-volume follow-up and invoice estimate

Thanks Sean — great recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Monthly volume (initial / expected / upside): 
  - Initial (Q3 pilot): ~150M–200M tokens/month
  - Expected (post-launch): ~350M–450M tokens/month
  - Upside (12mo): 700M–1.2B tokens/month (if usage and reranking expand)

- Budget / target unit economics: our procurement/cost team has signaled a target range of $4–$8 per 1M tokens for gen calls (we understand embeddings and rerankers are cheaper). If you have a recommended target $/1M tokens for committed plans, please include it in the estimate.

- A couple of technical asks for the cost model: 
  - Please show assumptions for prefix caching / KV reuse (we expect repeated prefixes for the assistant).
  - Indicate how the model accounts for peak vs. average latency SLAs (we care about 95th pctl).

Procurement timeline: we expect to have commercial terms and a PO by mid-April if the numbers align. Also, SOC2 evidence would be helpful for security review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alice
Alice Johnson
Director of Product, Acme Corp
alice.johnson@acmecorp.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmecorp.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme pricing / token-volume follow-up and invoice estimate

Hi Alice / Bob — attaching the cost model and a short invoice-style estimate per your request. High-level summary up front so it’s easier to scan: 

Summary (monthly expected band = 350M–450M tokens):
- Baseline list price (gen models): $12.00 per 1M tokens
- Proposed committed price (for 6–12 month commit at 350M+): $6.50 per 1M tokens (applies to generation tokens)
- Embeddings / reranker priced separately: $1.75 per 1M tokens (estimate)
- Estimated monthly spend (at 400M tokens, gen-heavy mix): 
  - Gen tokens (300M): $1,950/month (@ $6.50/1M)
  - Embedding/rerank tokens (100M): $175/month (@ $1.75/1M)
  - Total est: $2,125/month (~$25,500/year)

Notes on assumptions and unit economics (see attached spreadsheet for full line items):
- Compute baseline: includes GPU inference cost, autoscaling buffer (20%), and egress/storage where applicable.
- Caching/prefix reuse: we applied a conservative 15% effective token reduction on repeated prefixes for the assistant (documented in sheet cell 'cache_savings'). If you expect higher reuse, the unit cost can drop materially.
- Peak capacity / latency: estimate assumes target 95th pctl latency SLO of ~350ms for gen path using Dedicated or hosted with reserved burst. If you need lower p95, we’ll show a higher incremental cost.
- Discounts: additional volume tiers at 700M+ and 1B+ tokens reduce committed price to $5.25 and $4.25 per 1M respectively.

Attachments included:
- acme_cost_model_v1.xlsx (detailed assumptions, line-item compute + support)
- acme_invoice_estimate_v1.pdf (one-page invoice-style summary with payment terms)

Quick ask: can we schedule a 30-min call Tues/Wednesday next week (Mar 30/31) to walk through the model and confirm procurement steps? Also, if procurement expects PO by mid-April, we can prepare standard SOW/terms and begin onboarding docs now.

Drive link (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cAcmeCostModel
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/ACME-2026-001

Thanks — any immediate questions ping Marissa (SE) or David (SRE) — they’re cc’d.

Best,
Sean
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

Attachments:
- acme_cost_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- acme_invoice_estimate_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmecorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:41:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Acme pricing / token-volume follow-up and invoice estimate

Thanks Sean — got the spreadsheet and the one-pager. Quick notes after a skim: 

- Numbers look reasonable and the committed-price tiers align with our targets (we were hoping for ~$5–$6/1M at scale; $6.50 looks OK for initial commit).
- Can you expand the cache_savings scenario to show 25% and 40% reuse (sensitivity analysis)? That will help procurement model upside.
- Procurement wants to confirm whether the invoice includes support and onboarding fees or if those are one-time. Please spell those out in the invoice PDF.

We’re available for a 30-min call Wed 3/31 at 11am ET to review assumptions — does that work for your team? Also, procurement target is still mid-April for PO, so if you can send an SOW draft and standard terms this week that would be great.

—Alice
Alice Johnson
Director of Product, Acme Corp
alice.johnson@acmecorp.com
